items.stem: Why is a documented basis of estimate (BOE) essential to a professional estimate?

options.text: It records scope, assumptions, methods and exclusions so the estimate can be understood and validated
options.rationale: Correct: the BOE captures the assumptions, methods, scope and exclusions, making the estimate transparent and defensible.

options.text: It replaces the need for any cost data
options.rationale: A BOE documents the estimate; it does not replace underlying cost data.

options.text: It guarantees the project will be on budget
options.rationale: No document guarantees budget outcomes; the BOE supports understanding and validation.

options.text: It is only needed after the project finishes
options.rationale: The BOE is prepared with the estimate, not after project completion.

items.explanation: Correct: the BOE captures the assumptions, methods, scope and exclusions, making the estimate transparent and defensible.

items.stem: A parametric estimate uses a cost-per-square-metre factor from historical projects. What must be checked before applying it to a new project?

options.text: That the historical data is normalized and comparable in scope, time and location
options.rationale: Correct: parametric factors must be normalized for scope, escalation and location to be valid for the new project.

options.text: That the new project has exactly the same client
options.rationale: Client identity does not validate a parametric factor.

options.text: Nothing; historical factors always transfer directly
options.rationale: Factors require normalization; they do not transfer unadjusted.

options.text: Only that the currency symbol matches
options.rationale: Currency symbol alone ignores escalation, scope and location differences.

items.explanation: Correct: parametric factors must be normalized for scope, escalation and location to be valid for the new project.

items.stem: Which TWO are legitimate purposes of an estimate review before issue? (Select TWO)

options.text: Checking that scope, quantities and pricing are consistent and complete
options.rationale: Correct: review verifies completeness and consistency of scope, quantities and pricing.

options.text: Confirming assumptions, exclusions and contingency are documented and reasonable
options.rationale: Correct: reviewers confirm assumptions/exclusions and the reasonableness of contingency.

options.text: Lowering the total to match a desired number regardless of basis
options.rationale: Changing figures to hit a target without basis is unethical and invalid.

options.text: Removing the basis of estimate to simplify the package
options.rationale: The BOE must remain; removing it undermines defensibility.

options.text: Hiding known risks from the approver
options.rationale: Concealing risks falsifies the estimate's risk picture.

items.explanation: Correct: review verifies completeness and consistency of scope, quantities and pricing.
